engine: word timing (WORD-TIMING-v003 → review config captions + keyword icon pops); engine target jjv timing words (T-E33)
environment: ep04 review v013/v014, faster-whisper small.en word timestamps
symptom: Independent Q1 on v014: karaoke words that follow a pause light up before the sound — S02_A 'Where' lit at 2.66 s, voiced at 2.90 s (≈7 f early); S01_A 'look' 1.70 vs 1.86; S04_B 'I' 1.10 vs 1.22; also 'comes', 'cheese,', 'grow'. The user had approved v013 with the same timing; the v011 onset fix only moved the FIRST word of each line.
root_cause: Whisper word timestamps fill silence: a word after a pause gets a start at (or near) the end of the previous word, i.e. the gap start. The onset rule was applied only to line-first words, so inner words after pauses kept the gap-start time.
root_cause_status: measured (root RMS 20 ms windows on the receipt WAVs: < -65 dBFS until 2.88 s, voiced 2.90 s for 'Where')
fix_or_workaround: word-timing-v004: apply the onset rule to EVERY word — if the RMS at the word start is below the silence floor, move the start to the first sustained voiced window inside the word; never earlier, never past end-2 f; ends unchanged. v015 = v014 with only captions/icon-pop frames changed; same mix WAV remuxed, no audio change.
prevention: Q1 must measure every word (not samples, not only line-first) against an independent audible-onset detector, with a negative control. Engine T-E33 `jjv timing words` applies the onset rule per word. A user OK on an earlier cut does not prove word sync; the automatic gate does.
